metadata.title: A new proof of a Liouville theorem for the one dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii equation

nodes.name: One-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii equation (GP)
nodes.statement: $\ii\partial_t\psi+\partial_x^2 \psi+\psi (1-|\psi|^2)=0$ on $(t,x)\in \RR^2$, with $\lim_{|x|\to\infty} |\psi(t,x)|=1$.
nodes.statement_clean: The 1D Gross-Pitaevskii equation with non-vanishing boundary conditions at infinity.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian / Energy
nodes.statement: $E(\psi)=\frac12\int(\partial_x\psi)^2+\frac14\int(1-|\psi|^2)^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Conserved energy of GP combining gradient and potential terms.

nodes.name: Energy space $\cE$
nodes.statement: $\cE = \{ \psi \in \cC( \RR ; \CC ): \psi'\in L^2(\RR), \eta \in L^2(\RR)\}$ with $\eta = 1-|\psi|^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Energy space for GP solutions, controlling derivative in $L^2$ and density modulation.

nodes.name: Norms and weight $\rho$
nodes.statement_clean: Weighted norms used throughout the paper, with $\rho=\sech$ as the exponential weight.

nodes.name: Distance on energy space
nodes.statement: $d(\psi_1,\psi_2)= (\|\psi_1'-\psi_2'\|_\cH^2+\|\eta_1-\eta_2\|^2)^{1/2}$, making $(\cE,d)$ a complete metric space.
nodes.statement_clean: Distance giving $\cE$ a complete metric structure (following GS15).

nodes.name: Traveling waves $U_c$ (dark and black solitons)
nodes.statement: For $c\in(-\sqrt2,\sqrt2)$, $U_c=R_c+\ii I_c$ with $R_c(x)=\sqrt{(2-c^2)/2}\,\tanh(\sqrt{2-c^2}\,x/2)$ and $I_c=c/\sqrt2$; black if $c=0$, dark otherwise.
nodes.statement_clean: Explicit family of dark/black soliton profiles solving $-\ii cU_c'+U_c''+U_c(1-|U_c|^2)=0$.

nodes.name: Soliton density $Q_c$ and operators $L_\pm, S_c, S_c^\star$
nodes.statement: $\beta=\sqrt{2-c^2}$, $Q_c=1-|U_c|^2=\frac{\beta^2}{2}\sech^2(\beta x/2)$; $L_+=-\partial_x^2+\beta^2-3Q_c$, $L_-=-\partial_x^2+c^2-Q_c$, $S_c=\partial_x+\sqrt2 R_c=Q_c\partial_x Q_c^{-1}$, $S_c^\star=-\partial_x+\sqrt2 R_c=-Q_c^{-1}\partial_x Q_c$.
nodes.statement_clean: Linearized operators around $U_c$ together with the first-order operators $S_c$, $S_c^\star$ used for the factorization.

nodes.name: Functional $\cN$ for the transformed problem
nodes.statement: $\cN = (\int w_1^2+\int (\partial_x w_2)^2+ \int (\partial_x^2 w_2)^2)^{1/2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Hilbert-norm-like functional controlling the size of $(w_1,w_2)$ in the transformed coordinates.

nodes.name: Virial functional $\cI$
nodes.section: 5 Virial identity for the transformed problem
nodes.statement: $\cI=\int x (\partial_x w_2)(w_1-c\partial_x w_2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bounded virial-type functional whose time derivative will be coercive in $\cN$.

nodes.name: Liouville theorem for (GP) (Béthuel-Gravejat-Smets / Gravejat-Smets)
nodes.statement: Under uniform spatial decay $\inf_{a}\{|\eta(t,x+a)|+\sum_{k=1,2,3}|\partial_x^k\psi(t,x+a)|\}\leq Me^{-\gamma|x|}$ and closeness $d(\psi(0),U_{c_0})\leq\alpha_0$, any smooth solution of (GP) is a single traveling wave: $\psi(t,x)=U_{c_1}(x-c_1t+a_1)$.
conclusions: There exist $c_1\in(-\sqrt2,\sqrt2)$ and $a_1\in\RR$ such that $\psi(t,x)=U_{c_1}(x-c_1t+a_1)$ on $\RR\times\RR$

nodes.name: Modulation around traveling wave
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{th:1}, there exist smooth $a(t),c(t),\theta(t)$ such that $\psi(t,x)=e^{\ii\theta(t)}(U_{c(t)}(x-a(t))+\ep(t,x-a(t)))$ with three orthogonality conditions on $\ep$ and bounds $\|\ep\|_\cH+\|\zeta\|+|c-c_0|\lesssim\alpha_0$, $|\dot a-c|^2+|\dot c|+|\dot\theta|^2\lesssim\int\rho^\gamma|\ep|^2$.
conclusions: Existence of smooth modulation parameters $a,c,\theta$ and remainder $\ep$ with the orthogonality $\int\Re(U_c'\bar\ep)=\int\Re(\ii U_c'\bar\ep)=\int\Re(\ii R_c Q_c\bar\ep)=0$
Pointwise/integral bounds: $|\dot a-c|^2+|\dot c|+|\dot\theta|^2\lesssim\int\rho^\gamma|\ep|^2$ with $|\dot c|$ quadratic in $\ep$

nodes.name: Factorization identity for the linearized operator
nodes.statement: For any $c\in(-\sqrt2,\sqrt2)$, $L_+=S_c^\star S_c$ and $S_c(L_- - c^2)S_c^\star=(\partial_x^2-\beta^2)\partial_x^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{le:02} (factorization)
nodes.statement: First identity is standard from $L_+Q_c=0$. Second identity follows by computing $(L_- - c^2)S_c^\star=A\partial_x$ with $A=\partial_x^2-\sqrt2 R_c\partial_x-\sqrt2 R_c'$, then $S_cA=(\partial_x^2-\beta^2)\partial_x$ via the relations $2R_c^2=\beta^2-2\sqrt2 R_c'$ and $R_c''=-\sqrt2 R_c' R_c$.

nodes.name: First identity from $L_+Q_c=0$
nodes.statement: The identity $L_+=S_c^\star S_c$ is standard and stems from the fact that $Q_c$ lies in the kernel of $L_+$, i.e. $L_+Q_c=0$.

nodes.name: Compute $(L_- - c^2)S_c^\star = A\partial_x$
nodes.statement: Using $L_- - c^2=-\partial_x^2-\sqrt2 R_c'$ and $R_c''=-\sqrt2 R_c' R_c$, expand $(-\partial_x^2-\sqrt2 R_c')(-\partial_x+\sqrt2 R_c)=A\partial_x$ with $A=\partial_x^2-\sqrt2 R_c\partial_x-\sqrt2 R_c'$.

nodes.name: Compute $S_c A = (\partial_x^2-\beta^2)\partial_x$
nodes.statement: Using $2R_c^2=\beta^2-2\sqrt2 R_c'$ and $R_c''=-\sqrt2 R_c' R_c$, expand $(\partial_x+\sqrt2 R_c)(\partial_x^2-\sqrt2 R_c\partial_x-\sqrt2 R_c')=(\partial_x^2-\beta^2)\partial_x$.

nodes.name: Conclude second identity
nodes.statement: Combining $S_c(L_- - c^2)S_c^\star = S_c A \partial_x = (\partial_x^2-\beta^2)\partial_x^2$ proves the second identity.

nodes.name: Heuristic interpretation of the factorization (Remark~\ref{rk:2})
nodes.statement: For $c=0$, setting $w_1=S_0\ep_1$ and $\ep_2=S_0^\star w_2$, the system $\partial_t\ep_1=L_-\ep_2$, $\partial_t\ep_2=-L_+\ep_1$ becomes $\partial_t w_1=(\partial_x^2-2)\partial_x^2 w_2$, $\partial_t w_2=-w_1$, which is potential-free.

nodes.name: Inversion of $S_c^\star$
nodes.statement: For $f\in W^{1,\infty}(\RR)$ with $\int f Q_c=0$, the function $g(x)=\frac{1}{Q_c(x)}\int_x^\infty f Q_c=-\frac{1}{Q_c(x)}\int_{-\infty}^x f Q_c$ satisfies $S_c^\star g=f$, with pointwise and weighted-$L^2$ estimates $|g|+|g'|\lesssim\sup_{|y|\geq|x|}|f(y)|$, $|g'|+|g''|\lesssim\sup_{|y|\geq|x|}|f'(y)|+Q_c|f|$, and $\|\rho^\kappa g\|+\|\rho^\kappa g'\|\lesssim\|\rho^{\kappa/2}f\|$ for $0<\kappa<2\beta$.
conclusions: $g$ as defined satisfies $S_c^\star g=f$ and $g\in W^{2,\infty}(\RR)$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{le:03}
nodes.statement: Use $S_c^\star=-Q_c^{-1}\partial_x Q_c$ to verify $S_c^\star g=f$; integration by parts gives $g'(x)=-\frac{Q_c'}{Q_c^2}\int_x^\infty f'(y)\int_y^\infty Q_c\,dy+k_c(x)f(x)$ with $k_c(x)=-e^{-\beta x}$; weighted estimates follow from Cauchy-Schwarz and integration.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of bounded solution to $S_c^\star g = f$
nodes.statement: If $S_c^\star g=0$ then $Q_c g$ is constant, so the function $g$ in Lemma~\ref{le:03} is the unique bounded solution of $S_c^\star g=f$.

nodes.name: Transformed system in $(w_1,w_2)$
nodes.statement: $\partial_t w_1=(\partial_x^2-\beta^2)\partial_x^2 w_2+F_2$ and $\partial_t w_2=-w_1+2c\partial_x w_2+F_1$, where $w_1=v_1+cS_c w_2+\frac{1}{\sqrt2}|\ep|^2$ and $w_2$ is determined by $S_c^\star w_2=\ep_2$.

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev / Cauchy-Schwarz tools (Lemma~\ref{le:10})
nodes.statement: For $\kappa>0$ and $f\in\cE$, $\|f\rho^\kappa\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim\|f\|_\cH$, and for $A>0$, $\int_0^A f^2\rho^\kappa\lesssim\int_0^1 f^2+(\int_0^A(f')^2)^{1/2}(\int_0^A f^2\rho^{2\kappa})^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{le:10}
nodes.statement: First inequality: write $f(x)=f(y)+\int_y^x f'$, square, multiply by $\rho(y)$ and integrate. Second inequality: for $0\leq y\leq 1\leq x\leq A$ write $f^2(x)=f^2(y)+2\int_y^x f'f$ and apply Fubini and Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Coercivity bounds for $\ep_2$ via $w_2$ (Lemma~\ref{le:04})
nodes.statement: $\int(\partial_x\ep_2)^2+\int\ep_2^2\rho^\kappa+\|\ep_2^2\rho^\kappa\|_{L^\infty}+\int w_2^2\rho^\kappa\lesssim\cN^2$, and $|\partial_x w_2|+|\partial_x^2 w_2|\lesssim\sup_{|y|\geq|x|}|\partial_x\ep_2|+Q_c|\ep_2|\lesssim\rho^\gamma$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{le:04}
nodes.statement: Use the orthogonality $\int\ep_2 R_c Q_c=0$ together with $Q_c S_c^\star=-\partial_x Q_c$ to deduce $\int Q_c^2 w_2=0$, then derive $\int w_2^2\rho^\kappa\lesssim\int(\partial_x w_2)^2$. Bounds on $\ep_2$ and its derivative follow from $\ep_2=S_c^\star w_2$.

nodes.name: Orthogonality $\int Q_c^2 w_2 = 0$
nodes.statement: From $\int\ep_2 R_c Q_c=0$ and $Q_c\cdot S_c^\star=-\partial_x\cdot Q_c$, integration by parts gives $0=\int\ep_2 R_c Q_c=\int(S_c^\star w_2)R_c Q_c=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\int Q_c^2 w_2$.

nodes.name: Coercivity $\int w_2^2\rho^\kappa\lesssim\int(\partial_x w_2)^2$
nodes.statement: Standard coercivity argument from the orthogonality $\int Q_c^2 w_2=0$ yields the weighted $L^2$ control by $\int(\partial_x w_2)^2$.

nodes.name: Estimates on $\ep_2$ and $\partial_x\ep_2$
nodes.statement: From $\ep_2=S_c^\star w_2$, $|\ep_2|\lesssim|\partial_x w_2|+|w_2|$, hence $\int\ep_2^2\rho^\kappa\lesssim\int(\partial_x w_2)^2$. Differentiating yields $\partial_x\ep_2=-\partial_x^2 w_2+\sqrt2 R_c\partial_x w_2+Q_c w_2$, controlling $\int(\partial_x\ep_2)^2$ by $\cN^2$.

nodes.name: Pointwise decay of $\partial_x w_2,\partial_x^2 w_2$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{le:03} and Lemma~\ref{le:01} to obtain $|\partial_x w_2|+|\partial_x^2 w_2|\lesssim\sup_{|y|\geq|x|}|\partial_x\ep_2|+Q_c|\ep_2|\lesssim\rho^\gamma$.

nodes.name: Coercivity bounds for $\ep_1$ via $w_1$ (Lemma~\ref{le:05})
nodes.statement: $\int(\partial_x\ep_1)^2\rho^\kappa+\int\ep_1^2\rho^\kappa+\|\ep_1^2\rho^\kappa\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim\cN^2$, and $|w_1(x)|\lesssim|\partial_x\ep_1(x)|+\sup_{|y|\geq|x|}|\partial_x\ep_2(y)|+Q_c(x)|\ep_2(x)|+|\zeta(x)|\lesssim\rho^\gamma$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{le:05}
nodes.statement: Express $S_c\ep_1=Q_c\partial_x(\ep_1/Q_c)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\ep_1^2+h$ with $h=w_1-cS_c w_2-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\ep_2^2$, integrate to recover $\ep_1$ in terms of $h$, use orthogonality $\int\ep_1 Q_c=0$ to bound the integration constant $b$, then derive $\int\ep_1^2\rho^\kappa\lesssim\int h^2\rho^{\kappa/2}\lesssim\int w_1^2+\int(\partial_x w_2)^2$ via Lemmas~\ref{le:10},~\ref{le:01},~\ref{le:04}.

nodes.name: Set up integral representation of $\ep_1$
nodes.statement: From $v_1=S_c\ep_1=Q_c\partial_x(\ep_1/Q_c)$ and the definition of $w_1$, write $S_c\ep_1=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\ep_1^2+h$ with $h=w_1-cS_c w_2-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\ep_2^2$, then integrate on $[0,x]$: $\ep_1=bQ_c+Q_c\int_0^x\ep_1^2/Q_c+Q_c\int_0^x h/Q_c$.

nodes.name: Bound integration constant $b$ via orthogonality
nodes.statement: Using $\int\ep_1 Q_c=0$ together with Fubini and Cauchy-Schwarz, $|b|\lesssim\int\ep_1^2 Q_c+(\int h^2 Q_c^{3/2})^{1/2}$, and Lemma~\ref{le:10} gives $b^2\lesssim\alpha_0\int\ep_1^2 Q_c^2+\int h^2 Q_c^{3/2}$.

nodes.name: Weighted $L^2$ bound on $\ep_1$
nodes.statement: Cauchy-Schwarz, Lemma~\ref{le:10} and absorption of $\alpha_0$ on the left side give $\int\ep_1^2\rho^\kappa\lesssim\int h^2\rho^{\kappa/2}$, and the expression of $h$ together with Lemma~\ref{le:04} yields $\int\ep_1^2\rho^\kappa\lesssim\int w_1^2+\int(\partial_x w_2)^2$.

nodes.name: Bound on $\partial_x\ep_1$ and pointwise estimate on $w_1$
nodes.statement: Use $\partial_x\ep_1=-w_1+2c\partial_x w_2+\sqrt2 R_c\ep_1+c\ep_2+\frac{1}{\sqrt2}|\ep|^2$ to bound $\int(\partial_x\ep_1)^2\rho^\kappa$ by $\int w_1^2+\int(\partial_x w_2)^2$, and use $w_1=\partial_x\ep_1+2c\partial_x w_2+\zeta/\sqrt2$ together with Lemmas~\ref{le:01}-\ref{le:04} to get the pointwise estimate.

nodes.name: Estimates on parameter derivatives and forcing terms (Lemma~\ref{le:06})
nodes.statement: $|\dot a-c|^2+|\dot c|+|\dot\theta|^2\lesssim\cN^2$ and $\|\rho^{\gamma/4}\partial_x F_1\|\lesssim\cN^2$. Moreover $F_2=F_{2,1}+\partial_x F_{2,2}$ with $\|\rho^{\gamma/4} F_{2,1}\|+\|\rho^{\gamma/4} F_{2,2}\|\lesssim\cN^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{le:06}
nodes.statement: Combine Lemmas~\ref{le:01},~\ref{le:04},~\ref{le:05} for the parameter bound. For $\partial_x F_1$, decompose $\Theta_1=\Theta_{1,1}+\Theta_{1,2}$ using $S_c^\star 1=\sqrt2 R_c$ to remove the linear-in-$\cN$ contribution. For $F_2$, substitute $\partial_t\ep_i$ and split into quadratic terms and a derivative.

nodes.name: Parameter derivatives bound
nodes.statement: From Lemmas~\ref{le:01},~\ref{le:04},~\ref{le:05}, $|\dot a-c|^2+|\dot c|+|\dot\theta|^2\lesssim\int|\ep|^2\rho^\gamma\lesssim\cN^2$.

nodes.name: Estimate $\partial_x F_1$
nodes.statement: Bound $\|\rho^{\gamma/4}\partial_x P_1\|$ via $\|\rho^{\gamma/8}W\|\lesssim\cN^3$ and $\|\rho^{\gamma/8}N_1\|\lesssim\cN^2$ from Lemmas~\ref{le:04},~\ref{le:05}. Use $S_c^\star 1=\sqrt2 R_c$ to show $\Theta_{1,2}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\dot\theta$ has zero derivative, leaving only the quadratic contribution from $\Omega_{1,1}$.

nodes.name: Decomposition $F_2=F_{2,1}+\partial_x F_{2,2}$ and estimate
nodes.statement: Substitute $\partial_t\ep_i$ in the expression of $F_2$ and split into a non-derivative part $F_{2,1}$ and a derivative part $\partial_x F_{2,2}$ (using $S_c R_c'=0$); all surviving terms are quadratic, hence $\|\rho^{\gamma/4}F_{2,1}\|+\|\rho^{\gamma/4}F_{2,2}\|\lesssim\cN^2$.

nodes.name: Virial identity for the transformed problem (Lemma~\ref{le:07})
nodes.section: 5 Virial identity for the transformed problem
nodes.statement: $\dot{\cI}=\frac12\cQ+\cR$ where $\cQ=\int(w_1-2c\partial_x w_2)^2+\beta^2\int(\partial_x w_2)^2+3\int(\partial_x^2 w_2)^2$ and $\cR=\int x(\partial_x w_2)F_2+\int x(\partial_x F_1)(w_1-2c\partial_x w_2)-\dot c\int x(\partial_x w_2)^2$.
conclusions: $\cR=\int x(\partial_x w_2)F_2+\int x(\partial_x F_1)(w_1-2c\partial_x w_2)-\dot c\int x(\partial_x w_2)^2$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{le:07}
nodes.section: 5 Virial identity for the transformed problem
nodes.statement: Differentiate $\cI$ under the time evolution, substitute $\partial_t w_1$ and $\partial_t w_2$ from the transformed system, and integrate by parts to obtain the explicit decomposition $\cQ+\cR$.

nodes.name: Coercivity $\cQ\geq\frac{\beta^2}{16}\cN^2$ (Lemma~\ref{le:08})
nodes.section: 5 Virial identity for the transformed problem
nodes.statement: $\cQ\geq\frac{\beta^2}{16}\cN^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{le:08}
nodes.section: 5 Virial identity for the transformed problem
nodes.statement: With $b=\sqrt{1+7c^2/2}$, rewrite $\cQ=\frac{\beta^2}{2b}\int w_1^2+\frac{\beta^2}{2}\int(\partial_x w_2)^2+3\int(\partial_x^2 w_2)^2+\int(\frac{2c}{b}w_1-b\partial_x w_2)^2$, which is sufficient.

nodes.name: Cubic remainder estimate $|\cR|\lesssim\cN^3$ (Lemma~\ref{le:09})
nodes.statement: $|\cR|\lesssim\cN^3$.

nodes.name: Loss in cubic estimate
nodes.statement: Formally $\cR$ is quadratic and one might expect $|\cR|\lesssim\cN^4$, but some loss is necessary to recover space decay through Lemmas~\ref{le:04} and~\ref{le:05}, giving the cubic bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{le:09}
nodes.statement: Decompose $\cR=\cR_1+\cR_2+\cR_3$ with $\cR_1=\int x(\partial_x w_2)F_2$, $\cR_2=\int x(\partial_x F_1)(w_1-2c\partial_x w_2)$, $\cR_3=-\dot c\int x(\partial_x w_2)^2$, and bound each by Cauchy-Schwarz with the weighted estimates of Lemmas~\ref{le:04},~\ref{le:05},~\ref{le:06}.

nodes.name: Estimate of $\cR_1$
nodes.statement: Use the splitting $F_2=F_{2,1}+\partial_x F_{2,2}$, integrate by parts the term with $\partial_x F_{2,2}$, and apply Cauchy-Schwarz with weights to control by $\cN^3$ via Lemmas~\ref{le:04} and~\ref{le:06}.

nodes.name: Estimate of $\cR_2$
nodes.statement: By Cauchy-Schwarz, $|\cR_2|\lesssim\|\rho^{\gamma/4}\partial_x F_1\|(\|\rho^{-\gamma/4}xw_1\|+\|\rho^{-\gamma/4}x\partial_x w_2\|)\lesssim\cN^3$ via Lemmas~\ref{le:04},~\ref{le:05},~\ref{le:06}.

nodes.name: Estimate of $\cR_3$
nodes.statement: From Lemma~\ref{le:04}, $\int|x|(\partial_x w_2)^2\lesssim\cN$, and $|\dot c|\lesssim\cN^2$ from Lemma~\ref{le:06}, hence $|\cR_3|\lesssim\cN^3$.

nodes.name: New proof of Theorem~\ref{th:1} via factorization and virial
nodes.statement: Combining Lemmas~\ref{le:07},~\ref{le:08},~\ref{le:09} for $\alpha_0$ small gives $\dot\cI\gtrsim\cN^2$. Integration in time and the bound on $\cI$ yield $\int_\RR\cN^2<\infty$, hence a sequence $t_n\to\infty$ with $\cN(t_n)\to0$. Lemmas~\ref{le:04} and~\ref{le:05} then give $\|\ep(t_n)\|_\cH\to0$, and the orbital stability statement concludes that $\psi$ is exactly a soliton.

nodes.name: Combine virial, coercivity, cubic bound
nodes.statement: From $\dot\cI=\frac12\cQ+\cR$ (Lemma~\ref{le:07}), $\cQ\geq\frac{\beta^2}{16}\cN^2$ (Lemma~\ref{le:08}), and $|\cR|\lesssim\cN^3$ (Lemma~\ref{le:09}), for $\alpha_0$ (hence $\cN$) small enough, $\dot\cI\gtrsim\cN^2$.

nodes.name: Time integration and bound on $\cI$
nodes.statement: Integration of $\dot\cI\gtrsim\cN^2$ on $\RR$, together with the uniform bound on $\cI$ from Lemmas~\ref{le:04} and~\ref{le:05}, yields $\int_\RR\cN^2(t)\,dt<\infty$.

nodes.name: Subsequence $t_n\to\infty$ with $\cN(t_n)\to0$
nodes.statement: Since $\int_\RR\cN^2<\infty$, there exists $t_n\to+\infty$ with $\cN(t_n)\to0$.

nodes.name: Convergence to soliton in $\cE$ and conclusion
nodes.statement: By Lemmas~\ref{le:04},~\ref{le:05}, $\|\ep(t_n)\|_\cH\to0$; the pointwise decay of $\eta$ from Lemma~\ref{le:01} gives $\|\eta(t_n)-Q_{c(t_n)}\|\to0$, hence $d(\psi(t_n),e^{\ii\theta(t_n)}U_{c(t_n)}(\cdot-a(t_n)))\to0$. The orbital stability statement then forces $\psi$ to be exactly a single soliton.
